notes: Geochemistry regression set (audit item 7): exact counts that guard the data fixes (dedup, unit fixes, sample types). Truths are live SQL, so the expected numbers follow the database. Run: python evals/run_evals.py --set geochem_regression

questions.q: How many USGS (NGDB) geochemistry samples are in the database?

truth.n: SELECT count(*) FROM geochem.samples WHERE is_active AND source_system = 'USA_USGS_NGDB'

questions.judge: The headline count must match the truth (exact, or clearly flagged rounding) and the data source/publisher must be named. Extra context figures (results, analytes, breakdowns) are fine unless they contradict the headline count or each other; fail only on a wrong or missing headline count.

questions.q: How many different geochemistry datasets hold chemical analyses (not just ages or locations)?

truth.n: SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT source_system FROM geochem.samples WHERE is_active) s WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM geochem.analytical_results r WHERE r.source_system = s.source_system)

questions.judge: Gives the number of geochemistry source systems with chemical analyses matching the truth (15 at creation, including the GA deposit-geochemistry compilation that is not in the wide table; the Swedish bedrock-age points and the Wu zircon points have no chemistry). Listing them is fine.
